Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run** example of a small Rust CLI that

1. Reads the current clipboard text (Windows, macOS, Linux).
2. Sends that text to the ElevenLabs TTS API.
3. Streams the returned MP3 audio to your speakers.

> **TL;DR**  
> ```bash
> cargo new elevenlabs-tts
> cd elevenlabs-tts
> # copy the Cargo.toml and src/main.rs shown below
> cargo run
> ```

---

## 1. Prerequisites

| Item | How to get it |
|------|---------------|
| **Rust** | Install from <https://rustup.rs/> |
| **ElevenLabs API key** | Sign up at <https://elevenlabs.io> → *API* → *API Key* |
| **Voice ID** | In the ElevenLabs dashboard → *Voice Library* → click a voice → copy the `id` field |
| **Audio output** | Any system that can play MP3 (most OSes do). |

> **Tip** – Store the API key in an environment variable so it never ends up in source control.

```bash
# macOS / Linux
export ELEVENLABS_API_KEY="sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"

# Windows PowerShell
$env:ELEVENLABS_API_KEY="sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
```

---

## 2. Project layout

```
elevenlabs-tts/
├─ Cargo.toml
└─ src/
   └─ main.rs
```

### Cargo.toml

```toml
[package]
name = "elevenlabs-tts"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

# Optional: enable the `clipboard` feature on Windows only
[features]
default = ["clipboard"]

[dependencies]
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }
reqwest = { version = "0.12", features = ["json", "stream"] }
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
clipboard = { version = "0.5", optional = true }
rodio = "0.17"
anyhow = "1"
dotenvy = "0.15"
```

**1. How do I create a new document in Microsoft Word?**  
    To create a new document, open Word and click the **File** tab, then select **New**. You can choose a blank document or a template from the available options. Alternatively, press **Ctrl + N** on the keyboard to open a new blank document instantly.

**2. What is the difference between “Save” and “Save As” in Word?**  
    **Save** writes any changes to the current file, preserving its existing name and location. **Save As** creates a new file, allowing you to specify a different name, location, or file format (e.g., .docx, .pdf, .txt). Use **Save As** when you want to keep the original unchanged or convert to another format.

**3. How can I insert a table into a Word document?**  
    Place the cursor where you want the table, go to the **Insert** tab, click **Table**, and then drag to select the desired number of rows and columns. You can also click **Insert Table…** to specify exact dimensions or use the **Table Design** and **Layout** tabs to modify the table after insertion.

**4. What are the steps to apply a heading style to a paragraph?**  
    Select the paragraph, then on the **Home** tab choose a heading style (e.g., **Heading 1**, **Heading 2**) from the **Styles** gallery. This applies consistent formatting and enables automatic table of contents generation. You can modify the style by right‑clicking it and selecting **Modify**.

**5. How do I add page numbers to a Word document?**  
    Go to the **Insert** tab, click **Page Number**, choose the position (top, bottom, or margin) and alignment. For more control, select **Format Page Numbers…** to start numbering from a specific page or use a different numbering style. You can also insert page numbers in the header or footer via the **Header & Footer** tools.

**6. What is the purpose of the “Track Changes” feature?**  
    **Track Changes** records all edits—insertions, deletions, formatting changes—so reviewers can see what was altered. Activate it by clicking **Review** → **Track Changes**. Accepted or rejected changes can be managed through the **Accept** and **Reject** buttons, and the final document can be cleaned of tracked changes before distribution.

**7. How can I insert a hyperlink that opens a web page?**  
    Select the text or object you want to link, press **Ctrl + K** or click **Insert** → **Link** → **Insert Link**. In the dialog, type or paste the URL in the **Address** field, then click **OK**. The text will become a clickable hyperlink that opens the specified web page when clicked.
